Project example 01 · Deciding on your own

As much Git
as the work needs.

Anna has known her historical text for years. She wants to produce an edition with an introduction and commentary, but works alone, on a small budget and alongside other commitments.

Anna’s short route: clarify a question → record an action

01

A manageable beginning

Anna learns about TEI and oXygen and chooses a limited model with prepared support. She does not need to learn every technical possibility at once.

02

Record three things

Where is the authoritative working copy? How does she check and transfer changes? How can she start again on another computer? A short, versioned guide answers these questions.

03

The edition should be able to move with her

A university GitLab service can protect the edition files and history that Anna regularly transfers to it. Advice, software licensing, files outside the repository and later publication services are separate questions. Anna tests and documents recovery.

Remember

Even a one-person project needs understandable instructions, especially for your future self. They can be short.

How we would proceed

  1. Name the working location, editing tool and checking procedure.
  2. Record a meaningful change as a commit and transfer it to a reliable working host.
  3. Continue from a fresh copy and test the instructions as you go.

Done when: Anna can recover her latest transferred version and knows which additional files and services she needs.

A question for discussion

Which three pieces of information would help me resume work after a six-month break?
